title: Monabaugs (Westhampton)
summary: Monabaugs names a creek, swamp, and pond in the Westhampton area between Potunk and Ketchaponack Necks. The history preserves a water-place name in a landscape where coastal wetlands and waterways have changed over time.
address_label: Westhampton area between Potunk and Ketchaponack Necks, Southampton, NY
introduction_content: Monabaugs links a pond, swamp and creek within the Westhampton neck landscape. This cluster of water features helped people describe the land between Potunk and Ketchaponack. Tooker, pp. 139–140
history_content:
Records cited by Tooker mention a creek in 1683 and a swamp, pond and white oak in the 1686 divisions. The town record used Monabaugs as a boundary reference for both Potunk and Catchaponack. A tree could disappear and a wetland could change while its recorded name remained essential to understanding the earlier geography. Tooker, pp. 139–140

The 1686 town-book descriptions can be read together to compare the neighboring necks, waterways and crossings. Southampton town records, vol. II, printed pp. 113–114
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Monabaugs and Monobaugs. The name is interpreted as "a deep pond," using a form related to words for deep and pond or water-place. The possessive wording in the records may also preserve a personal name taken from the pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names of places are an important aspect of oral history as they become carriers of the past, allowing us a glimpse into occurrences in the past that history books often may have failed to mention.”

— Archive and Public Culture Research Initiative, University of Cape Town, Place Names of Pre-colonial Origin and their Use Today (2012), public project essay, oral-history paragraph
whereintheworld_content: The marker is an approximate reference between the historic Potunk and Ketchaponack necks. The 1686 record locates Monabaugs by adjoining necks and a pond-side tree, rather than coordinates. It has not been securely matched to a complete surviving pond-and-swamp outline, so no exact polygon is shown. Tooker, pp. 139–140
